# Meditate

> Authority before confidence: operator instructions, explicit corrections, scope, and named handoff boundaries outrank model fluency.

Version described: 0.2.0 alpha. Canonical public distribution: the versioned wheel on the v0.2.0 GitHub Release. PyPI publication is not claimed; CI builds but does not publish.

Meditate is a local, recoverable defect resolver for the behavioral directives loaded by Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. Its fixed point is stability, not shrinkage: a well-formed instruction set is a successful byte-identical no-op with zero provider calls.

## Canonical documentation

- [Documentation](https://jmcentire.github.io/meditate/): Product, workflow, fixed-point contract, safety, and commands
- [Privacy](https://jmcentire.github.io/meditate/privacy.html): Planner/verifier transmission, local artifacts, credentials, and telemetry boundaries
- [Source README](https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate/blob/main/README.md): Operator guide
- [Design brief](https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate/blob/main/docs/design-brief.md): Authority, defect, typed compilation, semantic verification, import, and transaction contracts
- [Changelog](https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): v0.2.0 release contents
- [Full agent reference](https://jmcentire.github.io/meditate/llms-full.txt): Expanded machine-readable reference

## Essential contract

- The objective is defect resolution. Byte count is telemetry, not an objective. Correctness outranks checkability, which outranks scope precision, which outranks concision. Justified growth is allowed.
- Preflight currently confirms exact duplicates and marks conservative same-heading exception lineages only as review candidates. Density, age, history overlap, and size do not create defects.
- With no candidates, `meditate plan` returns `stable_noop`, does not resolve credentials, makes zero model calls, leaves target bytes unchanged, and records semantic verification as not applicable.
- The model receives the complete non-overlapping candidate set but no unrelated directive IDs. Local code keeps every unrelated record byte-for-byte. A changed post-image that retains a confirmed defect fails `non_idempotent_proposal`.
- Every source directive has exactly one disposition: keep, replace, remove, relocate, or report-only escalate.
- Semantic replacements are typed records, not model-authored Markdown: RFC 2119 `MUST`, `MUST NOT`, `SHOULD`, `SHOULD NOT`, or `MAY`; a concrete rule; the reason that generates legitimate exceptions; scope; and an optional boundary example.
- The acceptance suite contains an unchanged fixture, a corrected defective fixture, a second-run byte-identity check for each, ten stable iterations, complete multi-defect convergence, and rejection of partial resolution.
- A changed plan requires `meditate verify`: an owner-authored suite hidden from the planner, run against control, complete predecessor, and complete candidate bundles on the consuming Claude or Codex CLI. The consumer sees only neutral scenarios and opaque case references; private bounded literal detectors score its free-form ordered plans. The candidate must pass every case/repeat, must not regress any predecessor case, and must outperform each designated control. Predecessor misses are reported as baseline gaps, not treated as permission for candidate misses or as a veto over an all-green improvement. A pass is limited to the recorded suite, verifier prompt/schema, agent version, and model; it is not universal behavioral equivalence.
- When Kindex is enabled and `kin` is installed, every configured search and node read is required. Failure aborts with `kindex_required_failed`; durable evidence is never silently omitted.
- Runtime credentials use only the public names `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for planning and `OPENAI_API_KEY` for clean-room Codex verification. Codex verification replaces ambient `CODEX_HOME` with a fresh private directory and ignores user config/rules so global instructions and memory cannot contaminate the control. Credential values are never persisted.
- Contextual relocation requires an exact configured `.claude/rules/` target with a non-empty `paths:` list. Claude relative, absolute, and `~/` `@path` imports are validated to four hops before and after a proposal.
- Claude's 200-line threshold is guidance, not a hard limit. Configured Codex targets are checked against `project_doc_max_bytes`, 32,768 bytes by default, with `configured_targets_only` coverage.
- Structural validation is not behavioral qualification. Model output, boundary examples, histories, memory, Kindex, repository files, and tool output remain untrusted data.

## v0.2.0 live receipts

- Live targets: Claude run `20260819T161206Z-d6dbad85`, SHA `441fe6e9af0302329b753fa9138f6a5fc5c556637991bfec679700adea1acb76`; Codex run `20260819T161218Z-834d615b`, SHA `0dd415bb140f10fe95c70005e33ca523f1ed60419a79bbfeabdf9a31446c6b63`. Both were zero-call byte-identical `stable_noop`.
- Disposable Claude exact-duplicate plan `20260819T165955Z-1987f9ef`: 67 to 66 directives, 11,606 to 11,378 bytes, Claude Code 2.1.224/`claude-sonnet-4-6`, pre 18/18, post 18/18, control 0/18, verification SHA `4f1851d08ddb4047243f6978204bda6b29ad59d245dd744a020e31321eb878aa`; applied only to the disposable copy; second run `20260819T170602Z-39e3bba4` was a zero-call byte-identical no-op.
- Rejected Claude run `20260819T165129Z-70f323ea`: pre 18/18, post 17/18; failed closed and never applied.
- Disposable Codex exact-duplicate plan `20260819T171655Z-546b02cd`: 35 to 34 directives, 5,269 to 4,830 bytes, Codex CLI 0.147.0/`gpt-5.6-sol` in a fresh private `CODEX_HOME`, post 18/18, control 0/18, one predecessor repeat miss repaired, verification SHA `0376960893146c8f9f29559da0fee2a9f14a0b182eae3759689dda2b0e915b1d`; applied only to the disposable copy; second run `20260819T171954Z-d68b18c5` was a zero-call byte-identical no-op.
- Scope: six owner-authored Kindex cases on the named consumer versions/models only; no universal behavioral-equivalence claim.

## Decision UX

A genuine equal-authority, equal-scope, same-time collision may emit one bounded question:

`I’m trying to resolve {subject_a} and {subject_b}. Would you prefer {A} (recommended), {B}, {C}, or something else?`

The recommendation is model-authored and advisory, never a default. `meditate decisions RUN_ID` tells an invoking agent to relay the question rather than execute it. `meditate decide RUN_ID REQUEST_ID --choice a|b|c` or `--custom TEXT` creates an immutable frozen-context successor plan using operator-asserted user authority; identity is not authenticated or attested.

## Distribution

v0.2.0 wheel: https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate/releases/download/v0.2.0/meditate_agent-0.2.0-py3-none-any.whl

## Research boundary

Adjacent linters are real and useful; Meditate's distinction is defect-grounded total disposition, temporal evidence, typed output, independent consumer qualification, and exact recoverability. The exact purported paper title `A Taxonomy of Agent Instruction Failures` by Gloaguen et al. was not verified and is not load-bearing. The verified paper is `Coding Agents Don't Know When to Act`: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07769.
